subject: Learning Methods
title: Sleep Stages and Memory
description: A quick win: understand Sleep Stages and Memory.

hook.text: Students who slept after studying remembered 40% more than those who stayed awake for the same duration.

buildup.text: Different sleep stages serve different memory types. Slow-wave sleep consolidates facts and events.

discovery.text: REM sleep consolidates procedural skills and emotional memories. Both stages are essential.

twist.text: Cutting sleep short means losing late-night REM. Skills learned yesterday never fully solidify.

climax.text: A full night of sleep is not a luxury for learners. It is when the brain finishes building memories.

punchline.text: Study, then sleep. The brain builds while you rest.

quiz.question: Which sleep stage consolidates facts and events?
